title: Box Breathing (4-4-4-4)
description: Navy SEAL square breathing technique to rapidly regulate the autonomic nervous system, calm racing heartbeat, and reduce acute panic or intense anger.
instructions: Inhale through nose for 4 seconds, hold breath for 4 seconds, exhale through mouth for 4 seconds, hold empty for 4 seconds. Repeat 4 cycles.

title: 5-4-3-2-1 Sensory Grounding
description: Sensory orientation exercise designed to detach the mind from overwhelm, dissociation, or acute anxiety by anchoring attention to immediate physical surroundings.
instructions: Acknowledge 5 things you can see, 4 things you can physically feel, 3 things you can hear, 2 things you can smell, and 1 positive thing you can taste.

title: Cognitive Thought Reframing
description: CBT-based mental restructuring prompt to challenge cognitive distortions, catastrophic assumptions, and emotional reasoning in high-pressure situations.
instructions: Write down the automatic negative thought. Identify the underlying cognitive distortion (e.g. all-or-nothing thinking). Formulate 2 objective, realistic alternative explanations.

title: Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR)
description: Systematic somatic tension release technique developed by Edmund Jacobson to relieve somatic stress, jaw clenching, and physical irritability.
instructions: Sequentially tense muscle groups (shoulders, hands, jaw, abdomen) for 5 seconds, then consciously release for 15 seconds, noticing the sensation of relaxation.

title: Pomodoro Micro-Break & Eye Rest
description: Short cognitive reset to mitigate screen fatigue, mental exhaustion, and sensory overload during demanding work blocks.
instructions: Step away from all screens. Look at an object 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Drink a glass of water and take 3 deep belly breaths before resuming.

title: Three Good Things Reflection
description: Positive psychology exercise proven to counterbalance negativity bias, cultivate optimism, and sustain team appreciation.
instructions: Write down three specific events from today that went well or that you appreciate, noting why each occurred and how it impacted you.

title: Physiological Sigh Reset
description: Neurobiological rapid calming breathing mechanism involving double-inhale followed by an extended sigh exhale to offload carbon dioxide and lower heart rate.
instructions: Take two consecutive inhales through nose (one deep, followed immediately by a quick sharp top-up), then slowly release a long, audible sigh through the mouth. Repeat 3 to 5 times.

title: Binaural Focus & Calming Soundscape
description: Curated ambient soundscape integrating nature acoustics and gentle low-frequency sounds to induce alpha brainwave relaxation and enhance focus.
instructions: Put on headphones, close eyes for the first 2 minutes, and allow the ambient soundscape to play in the background while working or resting.

title: Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
description: Urgent professional human counseling and confidential crisis intervention service for employees experiencing severe distress, acute trauma, or workplace burnout.
instructions: Connect immediately with a licensed mental health professional via our 24/7 dedicated confidential workplace support line or schedule an anonymous priority session.

title: Workplace Boundary & Communication Triage
description: Structured protocol for asserting professional boundaries, renegotiating unrealistic delivery dates, and de-escalating toxic workplace interactions.
instructions: Review our assertive communication templates. Identify tasks to delegate, defer, or decline using the non-violent communication framework: Observation, Feeling, Need, Request.

title: Desk Ergonomic Tension Release Stretch
description: Gentle seated physical stretches targeting neck stiffness, trapezius tension, and lower back compression caused by prolonged sedentary desk work.
instructions: Execute gentle neck rolls for 30s, clasp hands behind back to open the chest for 20s, and perform seated spinal twists gently on both sides.

title: Affect Labeling & Emotional Clarity
description: Neuroscience-backed technique of putting nuanced feelings into exact words (affect labeling) to dampen amygdala reactivity and clarify root causes.
instructions: Complete these 3 prompts: 1) The exact feeling I am having is... 2) The factual trigger without judgment was... 3) What I need to feel resolved is...

title: Outdoor Mindful Stroll
description: Low-intensity physical movement in natural light to reduce cortisol, stimulate divergent problem-solving, and relieve depressive stagnation.
instructions: Step outside for a 10-12 minute brisk walk. Leave phone notifications on silent. Pay deliberate attention to ambient sights, temperature, and bodily movement.

title: Informal Peer Sync & Social Connection
description: Casual, low-stakes human check-in with a trusted coworker or mentor to combat loneliness, isolation, and imposter syndrome.
instructions: Reach out to a friendly peer for an informal 15-minute coffee chat or virtual sync with no agenda other than human connection.

title: Win Log & Victory Anchoring
description: Positive reinforcement exercise to anchor feelings of accomplishment, pride, and psychological empowerment after milestones.
instructions: Record today's achievement in your professional brag sheet. Note who contributed and send a quick thank-you note to one collaborator.

title: 4-7-8 Relaxing Breath Meditation
description: Dr. Andrew Weil's parasympathetic tranquilizing breath pattern to soothe acute nervous system agitation and promote restful calm.
instructions: Inhale through nose for 4 seconds, hold breath for 7 seconds, exhale completely through mouth with a whoosh sound for 8 seconds. Repeat 4 cycles.

title: Mindful Beverage Ritual
description: Micro-mindfulness ritual focusing entirely on the sensory details of preparing and sipping warm tea, water, or coffee.
instructions: Prepare a warm drink. For 5 minutes, engage all senses: warmth against your hands, the aroma, steam rising, and the physical sensation of each sip.

title: Deep Diaphragmatic Belly Breathing
description: Belly breathing technique stimulating the vagus nerve to reverse the shallow thoracic breathing pattern caused by sustained workplace stress.
instructions: Place one hand on upper chest and one on abdomen. Breathe in so only the belly rises while chest remains still. Exhale slowly through pursed lips.

title: Cathartic Unfiltered Brain Dump
description: Expressive writing protocol to release pent-up resentment, disgust, or outrage without fear of judgment, followed by intentional closure.
instructions: Write non-stop for 7 minutes without filtering or editing grammar. Pour out raw feelings. Then tear or digitally delete the page as an act of release.

title: Core Values Compass Reflection
description: Alignment diagnostic to evaluate whether current workplace friction originates from value incongruence, guiding constructive renegotiation.
instructions: Identify which core value feels compromised (e.g. integrity, autonomy, fairness). Draft one constructive proposal to realign the situation.

title: Mindful Head-to-Toe Body Scan
description: Jon Kabat-Zinn MBSR body scan meditation to systematically release unconscious somatic holding patterns throughout the body.
instructions: Sit comfortably with eyes closed. Progressively bring curious, non-judgmental awareness to your toes, feet, legs, torso, chest, hands, neck, and face.

title: Isochronous Mood Elevation Playlist
description: Music therapy Iso-principle playlist starting with music that mirrors current sorrow, then gradually transitioning into empowering, hopeful harmonies.
instructions: Put on headphones and listen to the 3-track mood elevation sequence. Allow the progression of music to shift emotional inertia toward renewal.

title: Constructive 1-on-1 Workload Alignment
description: Collaborative manager alignment framework to proactively renegotiate conflicting deadlines and surface resource constraints before burnout occurs.
instructions: Schedule a short 1-on-1 with manager using the 'Traffic Light Priority' template: Green (critical), Yellow (can wait), Red (needs deprioritization).

title: Dr. Kristin Neff Self-Compassion Break
description: Evidence-based self-compassion exercise to counter the harsh inner critic when mistakes happen during demanding deliverables.
instructions: Place a hand over your heart. Say to yourself: 1) 'This is a moment of struggle.' 2) 'Struggle is part of being human.' 3) 'May I be kind to myself right now.'

title: Peer Shout-out & Gratitude Share
description: Team morale amplification exercise to celebrate mutual contributions and reinforce psychological safety across the organization.
instructions: Post a genuine shout-out in the team chat or send a recognition badge to a colleague who helped unblock work this week.
